## 🌎 Geopolitics

### US-China tariff truce extended to January 10 as rare earth competition intensifies

China extended its suspension of an additional 24% tariff on US goods through January 10, 2027, maintaining a 10% base rate while pausing expanded rare earth export controls for another two months. The US reciprocated by extending tariff exclusions and suspending ship port fees to the same date. China controls 91% of global refined rare earth output—the minerals critical for semiconductors, defense systems, and renewable energy—making the pause a strategic standoff rather than a resolution. Both sides have deferred $1.2 trillion in potential tariff hikes pending January negotiations.

**Why it matters.** India faces a two-front squeeze. First, India's own tariffs on US goods were slashed from 50% to 18% in February 2026 in exchange for halting Russian oil purchases—a deal now in tension as trade policy whipsaws. Second, Indian tech and defense firms depend heavily on Chinese rare earth imports; any escalation after January 10 could spike input costs and break supply chains your consulting clients in Hyderabad and Bangalore rely on. The tariff framework is also a macro signal: extended uncertainty in capital markets, potential inflation in imported inputs, and renewed trade war fears hitting Indian equities and rupee volatility.

**Action.** Track the January 10 deadline through USTR and Chinese Commerce Ministry statements. Monitor rare earth spot prices (REE indices on Bloomberg) as a leading indicator for India's tech export competitiveness. If you advise on quant or prop strategies, flag the US-China volatility cluster—equities, FX, commodities will all reprrice sharply if talks fail in January. Request a brief from your contacts on tariff implications for Indian IT hardware supply chains and chipset availability.

### Trump demands "total victory" in Iran war as ceasefire talks collapse

Trump declared on November 11 that the US has already won the war against Iran but now demands "total victory," signaling readiness for renewed military strikes. Israeli PM Netanyahu is simultaneously pushing for immediate resumption of airstrikes, while the first US-Iran-Ukraine peace talks since February broke down in Abu Dhabi on November 12 with Russia refusing any demilitarized zone and demanding Ukraine surrender four contested oblasts. Washington sought a ceasefire; Moscow restated territorial maximalism and NATO ultimatums. The Strait of Hormuz remains partially blocked by Iranian forces, disrupting global oil flows and hitting refinery schedules worldwide.

**Why it matters.** India's energy security and rupee stability hang on the next 30 days. India is China's largest competitor for Iranian oil imports and has been buying directly despite US sanctions—a posture that tightens if Trump authorizes new strikes on Iranian oil infrastructure or shipping. Escalation would spike Brent crude (now already elevated), reverse any benefit from the OPEC+ output deal, and force Indian refiners to shift sourcing faster, raising import costs and feeding inflation. On the macro side, any surprise military action would trigger a risk-off flight-to-safety sell, hitting Indian equities and the rupee—exactly the kind of exogenous shock that derails quarterly earnings and breaks technical trading patterns your prop clients track.

**Action.** Set up a daily brief tracking Trump's Iran rhetoric and any IDF movement indicators (check Jerusalem Post, Debka File live updates). Request your network in Mumbai on India's Iranian crude stockpile levels and refinery contingency plans—if supplies tighten, watch for diesel rationing signals that precede currency weakness. For quant desks, build scenario models for a 50-70 USD/bbl spike (Brent breakeven for Iranian supply shock); that tail risk is underpriced relative to Trump's rhetoric temperature. Review your consulting retainer clients' India exposure to energy-intensive sectors (steel, cement, refining, chemicals) ahead of any Strait escalation news.

*Sources: [timesofisrael.com](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-11-2026/) · [timesofisrael.com](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-13-2026/) · [aljazeera.com](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/13/russia-and-ukraine-report-overnight-attacks-amid-us-diplomatic-push)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Claude Fable 5.2 Launches at 1M Context Window, Leads FrontierCode 2.0 Benchmark

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026, with a 1M-token context window and 128K output limit, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. On BenchLM's FrontierCode 2.0 leaderboard (November 12 snapshot), Fable 5.2 leads at 49.1%, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (45.5%) and GPT-6 Astra (42.8%).

**Why it matters.** A 1M context window fundamentally changes what's feasible in agentic systems, multi-document retrieval, and codebases. At this scale, developers can pass entire projects (or conversations with full history) to a single inference pass without splitting across multiple API calls. The flat pricing across the entire window, without tiering for context depth, removes the per-token cost penalty for long contexts—a structural change that makes context-heavy architectures economically viable for production agents. Fable 5.2's FrontierCode lead (a code-generation benchmark) signals capability gains in both reasoning and practical coding tasks.

**Action.** If you're building agentic systems or RAG pipelines, benchmark Fable 5.2 against your current model on your own retrieval-heavy workloads; the 1M window may eliminate batching logic. Run FrontierCode 2.0 tasks locally to verify the benchmark generalizes to your codebase patterns. Check whether your token-counting logic accounts for output tokens fairly in cost comparisons, since output pricing has widened relative to input.

*Sources: [[https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview)]([https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview)) · [[https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/frontiercode-2](https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/frontiercode-2)]([https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/frontiercode-2](https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/frontiercode-2)) · [[https://www.cometapi.com/en/models/anthropic/claude-fable-5-2](https://www.cometapi.com/en/models/anthropic/claude-fable-5-2)]([https://www.cometapi.com/en/models/anthropic/claude-fable-5-2](https://www.cometapi.com/en/models/anthropic/claude-fable-5-2))*

### Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Coding and Agents with Flat Long-Context Pricing

Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen around November 13, 2026, as a faster, lower-cost model optimized for coding and agentic workloads. It features flat pricing across long-context ranges and automatic model switching to optimize latency and cost. Developers can download and run the model's largest weights on sufficient GPU infrastructure, and it rolled out across AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini app, and Search.

**Why it matters.** Hydrogen signals Google's shift toward specialized frontier models rather than a single flagship—differentiating on task (coding/agents) and infrastructure (local weight access) rather than raw scale. Flat long-context pricing de-risks experiments where context length varies, addressing a core friction point for agentic architectures. The automatic model switching suggests Google is preparing models for closed-loop execution, where the system picks the right inference endpoint without manual intervention. Local weight deployment access, even if only for large checkpoints, is a significant strategic move toward developer control in production environments.

**Action.** Test Gemini 4 Hydrogen on your code-generation and multi-turn agentic benchmarks to measure latency and cost versus Opus/Fable. If you run custom models internally, investigate whether Google's weight-download program covers your hardware (GPU memory, inference engine compatibility). Plan for automatic model switching in your routing logic if you adopt Hydrogen; bake in A/B testing infrastructure so you can measure the trade-offs when the system switches models mid-session.

## 🇮🇳 India

### SEBI Mandates AI Accountability for Capital Markets Infrastructure Ahead of Framework Release

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed sweeping accountability rules requiring market infrastructure institutions and intermediaries to answer for outcomes produced by their AI tools. Public comments remain open until November 28, 2026. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced a tiered AI governance framework incorporating human oversight requirements, mandatory kill switches, and explicit data controls, aligned with international supervisory standards set by IOSCO.

**Why it matters.** For an AI engineer building advisory, risk-scoring, or trading systems for Indian fintech or wealth platforms, this signals a fundamental shift: your AI outputs become your liability, and your systems must be auditable to regulators. The kill-switch and human-in-the-loop mandates mean no pure automation—architecture decisions made today will either compress margins or attract capital from compliance-heavy fintech players who can absorb the operational overhead. The November 28 comment window is your window to flag implementation constraints before the framework hardens into rules.

**Action.** Download the SEBI consultation paper from the regulator's website and review the proposed AI governance scope (which institutions, which tool types). Cross-reference against IOSCO's AI supervisory toolkit. File comments before November 28 if your startup builds for capital markets; track which peers are filing their own feedback to gauge industry alignment on implementation costs.

*Sources: [[Outlook Business — SEBI AI accountability proposal](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/sebi-proposes-accountability-for-ai-use-by-market-infra-institutions-intermediaries)]([Outlook Business — SEBI AI accountability proposal](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/sebi-proposes-accountability-for-ai-use-by-market-infra-institutions-intermediaries)) · [[MoneyLife — SEBI AI mandates for markets](https://www.moneylife.in/article/ai-in-markets-sebi-to-mandate-human-oversight-kill-switches-and-data-controls-says-pandey/81406.html)]([MoneyLife — SEBI AI mandates for markets](https://www.moneylife.in/article/ai-in-markets-sebi-to-mandate-human-oversight-kill-switches-and-data-controls-says-pandey/81406.html)) · [[Policy Edge — November timeline analysis](https://www.policyedge.in/p/sebi-targets-wider-clearing-by-november-prepares-ai-rules-for-market-firms)]([Policy Edge — November timeline analysis](https://www.policyedge.in/p/sebi-targets-wider-clearing-by-november-prepares-ai-rules-for-market-firms))*

### Razorpay Clears SEBI IPO Hurdle, Eyes $500M–600M Public Float at $5B Valuation by 2027

Payment processor Razorpay has received Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) approval for an initial public offering, under the regulator's confidential pre-filing route, giving the company up to 18 months to launch. The company is targeting ₹3,750–4,500 crore ($500M–600M USD) from the public markets at a $5 billion valuation. The approval arrives amid parallel regulatory scrutiny: the Karnataka High Court rejected a petition by Razorpay senior executives seeking to quash an SFIO complaint over alleged merchant onboarding and KYC lapses.

**Why it matters.** Razorpay's approval signals that fintech IPOs remain in the SEC's sights despite compliance friction. For engineers at Indian payment infrastructure, lending platforms, and SaaS-for-fintech companies, this opens a template: founders and early employees can now chart an IPO path without waiting for the regulatory landscape to become hostile. The concurrent SFIO case shows regulators will greenlight IPOs while investigations are ongoing—the bar is procedural correctness, not a clean slate. This unblocks growth-stage fintech recruiting and capital raises.

**Action.** Track when Razorpay files its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI—likely within 12 months—to study the disclosure depth regulators now expect from a payment platform IPO. If your fintech operates payment flows, shadow Razorpay's compliance filings to audit your own KYC and merchant-onboarding documentation; SFIO flags will be common. Monitor which other fintechs (lending, b2b-pay) file for IPO approvals in the next quarter, as the Razorpay approval may trigger a wave.

*Sources: [[Inc42 — SEBI clears MakeMyTrip and Razorpay IPOs](https://inc42.com/buzz/sebi-clears-makemytrips-india-ipo/)]([Inc42 — SEBI clears MakeMyTrip and Razorpay IPOs](https://inc42.com/buzz/sebi-clears-makemytrips-india-ipo/)) · [[CIOL — Razorpay IPO approval amid SFIO case](https://www.ciol.com/news/razorpay-sebi-ipo-approval-karnataka-hc-sfio-case-12807606)]([CIOL — Razorpay IPO approval amid SFIO case](https://www.ciol.com/news/razorpay-sebi-ipo-approval-karnataka-hc-sfio-case-12807606)) · [[NewsBytes — SEBI IPO approvals roundup](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/sebi-clears-ipos-for-sembcorp-green-infra-razorpay-makemytrip-india/tldr)]([NewsBytes — SEBI IPO approvals roundup](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/sebi-clears-ipos-for-sembcorp-green-infra-razorpay-makemytrip-india/tldr))*

## 📈 Markets

### Nvidia's CEO Exit Cracks Tech, Pulling US and India Markets Lower

US equities fell as Nvidia shocked the sector with CEO Jensen Huang's surprise resignation, sending the Nasdaq down 229.82 points (-0.91%) to 25,136.27 while the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points (-0.40%) to 7,561.67. The Dow managed a modest gain, closing at 52,347.55 (+0.10%). India's benchmark indices echoed the weakness: the Sensex dropped 318.56 points (-0.39%) to 81,592.45, while the Nifty 50 fell 155.05 points (-0.61%) to 25,144.30, snapping a three-day winning streak. Brent crude hovered near $96 a barrel, stoking fresh inflation fears in New Delhi.

**Why it matters.** Nvidia's leadership vacuum ripples across AI infrastructure globally. For India, the tech selloff arrives as oil pressure already threatens rupee stability and RBI flexibility. With crude elevated and US equities cooling after weeks of AI-driven strength, the carry-trade unwind that supported emerging markets becomes asymmetric—US tech correction but oil burden stays. If Nvidia chaos extends into next week, foreign portfolio inflows to India could reverse, testing whether the Nifty can hold 25,000 support or slide toward 24,800. The RBI's "calibrated tightening" stance faces a narrower bandwidth if global yields spike on risk-off.

**Action.** Monitor US tech earnings revisions; Nvidia's November 20 earnings will set the tone. Watch whether US yields (currently ~4.93% on the 10Y, per early November data) drift higher on recession fears, which would force Indian G-Sec yields higher in tandem. The next RBI signals will matter if the Fed signals dovishness or holds. Track oil—if Brent breaks below $90, inflation pressure eases for India and the rupee could stabilize; above $98 locks in RBI constraints.

### Oil Rebound Revives Inflation Specter; Crude at $96 Pressures Indian Rupee and RBI Timing

Brent crude rebounded to near $96 per barrel after touching a ten-week low of $91.50 on November 10, amplifying inflation concerns in India just as the RBI shifts into "calibrated tightening" mode. Gold, meanwhile, retreated to $3,881.75 per ounce, down 5.45% over the month. MCX gold in rupees stayed near Rs 1,39,160 per 10 grams, reflecting the rupee's pressure from import-driven oil bills. Indian exporters faced headwinds as crude strength compounds the carry-trade unwind and limits the RBI's ability to cut or hold rates.

**Why it matters.** Oil volatility is the critical variable for India's twin balance: inflation and rupee. At $96, crude is nowhere near the $80–$85 band that would ease inflation and let the RBI pivot to easing. Instead, elevated oil forces the RBI to maintain a hawkish bias longer, squeezing real rates for borrowers and capping equity multiples. For quant prop players, the correlation between oil and USDINR is the arb: if WTI/Brent climbs further (to $100+), rupee weakness accelerates and the RBI may be forced into a "surprise" hike to defend the currency, much as it did in 2023. Watch if OPEC+ signals production cuts or if geopolitical risks (Middle East, Russian supply) reignite.

**Action.** Set alerts: crude above $98 and rupee below 94.50 signal an RBI hike is imminent. If crude falls below $90, the RBI gains space to stay on pause through Q4 and Q1. Track the RBI's next monetary policy (likely December 2026); the November 13 close suggests the market has priced in one more hold, but oil >$100 would flip expectations into a 25bp hike. For traders, long UST 10Y / short India G-Sec 10Y (the 250bp spread is tight) could widen if oil reignites.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Trusted Space Acquires Falcon ExoDynamics to Command Autonomous Satellite Fleets

Trusted Space, a Virginia-based space autonomy software company backed by Washington Harbour Partners, acquired Falcon ExoDynamics on November 12 to combine mission-level and vehicle-level autonomy for national security satellites. Falcon ExoDynamics, founded in 2017 and based in El Segundo, builds maneuverable spacecraft control software. Terms were undisclosed, but the deal pairs Falcon's vehicle autonomy with Trusted Space's mission-level command-and-control platform, a capability gap military space operators face as satellite constellations grow faster than personnel.

**Why it matters.** Defense deeptech is moving from single-platform autonomy toward orchestrated multi-satellite autonomy. Trusted Space's CEO Robert MacMillan frames it plainly: a small cadre of Space Force guardians will manage exponentially more orbital assets. The pattern here mirrors a consolidation playbook in edge infrastructure and autonomous systems where point-solution startups sell to platform-builders that can own the full decision stack. Falcon ExoDynamics had just won a $24 million SDA/DIU award in August for on-orbit servicing; this acquisition signals that venture-backed autonomy stacks have become acquisition targets for incumbents building national security infrastructure.

**Action.** Track Trusted Space's orbital roadmap and the next Air Force Satellite Communications (MILSATCOM) contract bids. The company's August $15 million AFRL award is the clearest public signal of budget flow; monitor SeaPort-e and SAM.gov for Trusted Space engineering buys. Read Axios' original reporting and watch for Falcon ExoDynamics' team joining Trusted Space's engineering org to measure integration velocity.

### IBM Acquires Indian Identity Security Startup AuthMind to Monitor AI Agent Credentials

IBM announced on November 12 that it acquired AuthMind, an Indian identity security company specializing in monitoring how AI agents and autonomous systems use credentials after access is granted. IBM said the acquisition expands security monitoring for its HashiCorp Vault platform, a critical piece of enterprise secret management. Financial terms were not disclosed, though IBM Ventures had previously invested in AuthMind's seed round in 2023, signaling existing strategic alignment.

**Why it matters.** As enterprises deploy agentic AI into production, credential sprawl becomes a security blind spot. AuthMind's hook is post-access monitoring: it logs what actions AI agents take once they have credentials, allowing security teams to revoke unsafe access in real time. This mirrors a decade-old pattern in identity: first-generation tools (Okta, Ping) shifted identity left, but modern systems need to shift monitoring right—into agent runtime. IBM embedding AuthMind into Vault gives customers observability they don't yet have, and Indian founders are increasingly building specialized security infrastructure plays for global platforms (Wiz, Snyk, and earlier rounds by Indian-founded teams in encryption and zero-trust).

**Action.** Watch for Vault release notes announcing AuthMind integration in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Read IBM's official acquisition statement for Vault roadmap signals. If you're evaluating AI agent governance, request a Vault demo focused on the AuthMind credential-monitoring feature rather than baseline secret rotation, which is table-stakes by now. Track IBM Cloud's agentic AI marketing; this acquisition is upstream of their larger enterprise AI push.

*Sources: [[Pulse2](https://pulse2.com/ibm-authmind-acquisition-expands-ai-agent-identity-security-in-hashicorp-vault)]([Pulse2](https://pulse2.com/ibm-authmind-acquisition-expands-ai-agent-identity-security-in-hashicorp-vault)) · [[VermoegensZentrum on AuthMind as Indian firm](https://www.vermoegenszentrum.ch/en/stock-exchange-and-markets/news/ibm-acquires-indian-identity-security-firm-authmind)]([VermoegensZentrum on AuthMind as Indian firm](https://www.vermoegenszentrum.ch/en/stock-exchange-and-markets/news/ibm-acquires-indian-identity-security-firm-authmind)) · [[InfotechLead](https://infotechlead.com/analytics/tech-ma-deals-ibm-authmind-trusted-space-falcon-exodynamics-worker-ai-deltagen-99600)]([InfotechLead](https://infotechlead.com/analytics/tech-ma-deals-ibm-authmind-trusted-space-falcon-exodynamics-worker-ai-deltagen-99600))*

## 🩹 Health & Science

### ANGPTL4 Antibody Cuts Triglycerides by Up to 72% in Phase 2b Trial

Marea Therapeutics reported November 12 in NEJM that MAR001, a monoclonal antibody targeting ANGPTL4, reduced fasting triglycerides by 39.1–45.5% across three dose cohorts in a 24-week randomized trial of 235 patients with elevated triglycerides. In participants with baseline triglycerides above 500 mg/dL, reductions reached 57.4–72.2%, addressing a large population gap: statins don't adequately lower triglycerides, and current drugs carry safety trade-offs.

**Why it matters.** Elevated triglycerides independently predict cardiovascular and pancreatitis risk. ANGPTL4 inactivation is supported by human genetics (loss-of-function carriers have low triglycerides and lower CAD risk), so this antibody approach de-risks the target. For builders of AI-guided lipid management or cardiometabolic risk models, this establishes a validated mechanism that could become routine adjunct therapy, expanding the addressable market for digital prevention tools that identify high-triglyceride phenotypes.

**Action.** Read the NEJM paper (O'Donoghue et al., DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2612463) and the AHA Scientific Sessions presentation. The next lever is post-hoc analysis of cardiovascular events in existing cohorts with genetically-supported ANGPTL4 loss, and Phase 3 design that measures hard outcomes (MI, pancreatitis) rather than biomarker change alone. Clinical adoption hinges on long-term safety and event reduction—conversations with Marea about Phase 3 data timelines will signal whether this advances to standard-of-care.

*Sources: [[NEJM November 12, 2026](https://www.nejm.org)]([NEJM November 12, 2026](https://www.nejm.org)) · [[News-Medical report](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261109/New-monoclonal-antibody-therapy-significantly-lowers-patient-triglyceride-levels.aspx)]([News-Medical report](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261109/New-monoclonal-antibody-therapy-significantly-lowers-patient-triglyceride-levels.aspx)) · [[EurekAlert press release](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1150797)]([EurekAlert press release](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1150797)) · [[2 Minute Medicine summary](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/novel-inhibitory-antibody-mar001-lowers-triglycerides-and-remnant-cholesterol-in-humans/)]([2 Minute Medicine summary](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/novel-inhibitory-antibody-mar001-lowers-triglycerides-and-remnant-cholesterol-in-humans/))*

### RNA Blood Test Detects Precancerous Ovarian Lesions with 92% Sensitivity

Researchers at Hoag Family Cancer Institute published November 10 in Nature Medicine a blood-based RNA biomarker (Tu-Stroma) that identifies serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), the precancerous precursor of high-grade serous ovarian cancer. In validation cohorts, the marker achieved 92.3% sensitivity and 98.2% specificity for detecting fallopian tube lesions, years before invasive disease develops.

**Why it matters.** High-grade serous ovarian cancer is diagnosed late, with 60% presenting at stage III/IV. Early detection at the precancerous STIC stage—which remains anatomically confined—could unlock curative intervention. BRCA1/2 carriers face lifelong surveillance burden; a blood-based STIC detector eliminates false negatives from imaging alone and could shift management from prophylactic surgery toward targeted chemoprevention or more frequent screening in high-risk populations, reshaping ovarian cancer prevention pathways.

**Action.** Access the Nature Medicine paper (DOI 10.1038/s41591-026-04732-9) and contact Hoag or the authors about next-stage validation in prospective cohorts of BRCA carriers and high-risk women. The clinical bottleneck is prospective blinded validation and understanding STIC's progression kinetics (how many precancerous lesions become cancer, and on what timeline). Funding conversations should target precision oncology networks and hereditary cancer programs willing to enroll women for serial blood draws.

## 🎤 Culture & World

### Mungiu's Palme d'Or Prizewinner Fjord Opens in Theaters—Political Polarization Drama Arrives as Awards Play

Cristian Mungiu's "Fjord," which won the Palme d'Or at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival in May—the Romanian filmmaker's second top prize, placing him among only ten directors ever to have won twice—opens in limited release November 13, distributed by Neon. The film stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve and unfolds in Norway, centering on Evangelical Christians whose relocation triggers state intervention over parenting methods. The supporting cast includes Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, and Rupert Grint.

**Why it matters.** Fjord's November opening triggers Neon's seventh consecutive year backing the Palme winner, a streak that signals how thoroughly prestige arthouse distribution has consolidated around Cannes validation. The film's subject—religious families colliding with Nordic welfare state authority—captures a real wedge in contemporary politics (religious liberty vs. state protections), making it both a festival statement and a cultural document. For Neon, the release doubles as a statement that mid-budget, director-driven drama can still command theatrical space and awards infrastructure in 2026, a meaningful counterweight to franchise dominance.

**Action.** Watch whether Fjord reaches $10M+ domestic (a floor for prestige arthouse viability post-pandemic). Track reviews from major outlets to gauge how U.S. critics handle the film's religious-autonomy themes, which often polarize along the same fault lines the film depicts. The Awards Daily and IndieWire coverage will signal whether the trade expects a Best Foreign Film Oscar push.
